text: Claude Code keeps each conversation in ~/.claude , only on the machine where it happened, and by default deletes transcripts older than 30 days. Session Vault keeps an encrypted copy of the sessions you want to hold on to. A saved session survives that cleanup, a new laptop or a wiped disk, and you can fetch it on any of your machines and carry on where you left off. Get started /session-vault:save save the current session /session-vault:fetch restore a saved session here It's a Claude Code plugin, so both commands run inside Claude Code. Before uploading, the plugin encrypts the transcript with age , using a key created on your machine the first time you save. The server keeps the encrypted file plus what it needs to find it again: the session ID, the project, the folder it was saved from and an optional name. It can't read the conversation. To fetch on another machine, copy the key ( ~/.config/session-vault/age.key ) there. Keep a backup of it too: it's the only copy, and without it nobody can decrypt your sessions, us included. Plans differ only in how many sessions you can store. Saving a session again doesn't count as a new one. If you move to a smaller plan nothing is deleted; you just can't add sessions until you're under the new limit. The server is open source. If you'd rather keep your sessions on your own hardware, run it there and point the plugin at it. You won't need an account here. github.com/galeone/session-vault-server 1. Enter your email and we'll send you a link. The first time, it creates your account and shows you your token; after that it just signs you in. 2. Install the plugin in Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add galeone/session-vault-plugin /plugin install session-vault@galeone-plugins 3. Put your token in ~/.config/session-vault/config : SESSION_VAULT_URL=https://session-vault.dev SESSION_VAULT_TOKEN=your-token 4. Run /session-vault:save . The first save creates age.key in ~/.config/session-vault/ . Session Vault · Terms · Privacy · Source code
